mix.notes: Live color: convert the camera L*a*b* reading to RGB. Use hex as fallback.

frame.position: depends on component anchor: 'bottom' = center of footprint at the bottom face, 'center' = geometric center. Rotation (deg, X then Y then Z) is applied about the anchor.

container.notes: Owner, step 17: a tapered round tub, black opaque PP body, clear snap-on flat lid. Measured: bottom outer D79, top outer D113 at the lid, height 77 (taken as the closed tub, lid included). Every other number is an estimate until the tub is weighed and measured. How many tubs a batch fills and how much each holds belong to the order and the simulator (config/simulator.json "order"), not to the container.

Closed camera box, matte black (owner, step 17: it stays black), touching the control cabinet's left wall. Apart from the vessel again, as in the earlier design (owner, step 17). Inside: the camera, the flow cell, its white patch and the two LED strips. Size estimated.
Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3, straight on at 90 degrees to the flow cell window, lens 120 mm from it (doc 02); looks at the flow cell only (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17).

Small cell beside the vessel: printed white body, glass window toward the camera (parts list 2026-11-09). Owner, step 17, estimated: inside 40 x 40 x 10 mm, 10 mm from the glass to the white back, so the light crosses the liquid twice (20 mm). One port at the bottom, both ways; the vent tube to the vessel lid stays.
The liquid behind the glass shows the colour the camera read last.

White reference patch beside the window, outside the glass, the same white plastic as the cell (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17): every reading is taken relative to it, for lighting compensation.
White 12 V LED strip at 45 degrees to the window, so the glass glare misses the camera (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17).

DC pump, reversible (parts list 2026-11-09): forward fills the flow cell from the vessel through its bottom port, reverse returns the sample to the vessel. Behind the camera box, so its tubes run at the back (owner, step 17).
Raspberry Pi Camera Module 2 for the customer colour station, a planned feature (parts list 2026-11-09). Not installed; at the front, position estimated (owner, step 17).
Rigid rail under each belt. Takes press force.
Rigid rail under each belt. Takes press force.
JGB37-520 12 V gear motor, 60-100 rpm, one motor for both belts. Run/stop only: the PLC switches it through a relay; no speed control and no rotation sensor (parts list 2026-11-09).
E3F-DS30C4 at the end of the belt (parts list 2026-11-09). Until the tray is built, containers stop here; while it sees one, the belt stops until it is taken away (owner, step 17).
Push-pull solenoid 12 V at the bottom of the magazine; opens to release one container (parts list 2026-11-09, replaces the two-finger release). The PLC switches it through a relay. Size estimated.
Lift-and-weigh platform in the gap between the belts, on a 1 kg load cell, lifted by an MG996R servo (rack and pinion) so the container leaves the belts. Fits under the 79 mm base (owner, step 17).
MG996R servo, raises the platform by rack and pinion (parts list 2026-11-09).
Above the lifted container (top at 185), never touches it.
decision: 0 none, 1 pass, 2 reject. The lid drops while the platform is up; the press works only after it lowers (owner, step 17).
MG996R servo, raises the platform by rack and pinion (parts list 2026-11-09).
MG996R servo with a pusher: pushes bad containers off the belt toward the reject bin on the front side (parts list 2026-11-09).
Holds the lids (parts list 2026-11-09). A lid drops through a guide funnel onto the container (doc 02). Size estimated from the 113 mm lid.
Drop gate under the lid magazine: lets one lid fall while the container is still lifted (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17).
MG90S servo that opens the drop gate (parts list 2026-11-09).
Car central-lock actuator 12 V, switched by a 2-channel relay that swaps its polarity (parts list 2026-11-09). Presses the lid only after the platform lowered (owner, step 17).
KW12 micro switch: confirms the lid press reached the end (parts list 2026-11-09). Position estimated.
Reject bin, on the front (audience) side. Owner, step 17: 100 mm deep, narrower than the 113 mm container top (open item, doc 05).

6-slot tray that slides sideways on a rail, driven by a NEMA 17 stepper (parts list 2026-11-09); deferred, not installed (owner, step 17). Open (doc 05): 6 slots are fewer than the largest batch, and the tray needs more travel than the 800 mm table gives: drawn at home with slot 1 at the belt, it sticks out behind the table.
MGN12H rail.
GT2 belt with its pulley and idler.
NEMA 17 stepper with a TMC2209 driver.
KW12 home switch.
The control panel, white outside (owner, step 17): raised 100 mm on legs, cables enter from below through glands. Interior parts on the back panel; positions estimated.
Mushroom head, latching, 2 NC, 22 mm. Cuts the 12 V motor line through the contactor; the ESP32s stay powered.
Green, normally open (LA38-11, 22 mm).
Red, normally closed (LA38-11, 22 mm).
Yellow, normally open (LA38-11, 22 mm). Replaces the alarm acknowledge button (owner, step 17).
Tower light with buzzer LTA-205J 24 V: green, yellow, red (parts list 2026-11-09). 0 off, 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.
Inovance Easy320-0808TN: 8 digital inputs, 8 transistor outputs, 1 RS485, 2 Ethernet (parts list 2026-11-09). Owns the sequence, the limits and the alarms (doc 01). Size estimated.
GE20-4DI: 4 more inputs, 12 in all.
CJX2-0910Z, 24 V DC coil: cuts the 12 V motor line on e-stop.
DIN rail with the terminals and the fuse holders.
Terminals and fuse holders on the DIN rail.
4-channel 24 V relay board, low-level trigger: the conveyor motor and the infeed solenoid.
Raspberry Pi 5 4 GB with a 27 W supply and an RTC battery: the camera station, later also the gateway (parts list 2026-11-09). Currently dead: repair or replace.
Mean Well LRS-150-12: the 12 V motor line, after the contactor (parts list 2026-11-09).
Mean Well LRS-75-24: 24 V for the PLC, the sensors and the ESP32 stations.
Second DIN rail, for the three ESP32 enclosures (owner, step 17).

Station 1: the four dye scales (HX711) and the four dye pumps (TMC2209 drivers). An ESP32 DevKit V1 with a MAX3485 RS485 module, a terminal board and an LM2596 24 to 5 V buck (it stays on during an e-stop), in a printed DIN enclosure on the panel's second DIN rail (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17: "station 1" is the zone it controls, not a box at the line). Size estimated: three fit beside the 24 V supply only if each is about 48 mm wide.

Station 2: the big tank level, the vessel and filling scales, the base, water, filling, drain and sample pumps (D4184 MOSFET modules, the sample pump reversing driver), the mixer and the filling lift servo (XL4015 buck). An ESP32 DevKit V1 with a MAX3485 RS485 module, a terminal board and an LM2596 24 to 5 V buck (it stays on during an e-stop), in a printed DIN enclosure on the panel's second DIN rail (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17: "station 2" is the zone it controls, not a box at the line). Size estimated: three fit beside the 24 V supply only if each is about 48 mm wide.

Station 3: the check scale and lift servo, the reject pusher, the lid-drop servo and the lid press (2-channel relay), with an XL4015 buck for the servos. An ESP32 DevKit V1 with a MAX3485 RS485 module, a terminal board and an LM2596 24 to 5 V buck (it stays on during an e-stop), in a printed DIN enclosure on the panel's second DIN rail (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17: "station 3" is the zone it controls, not a box at the line). Size estimated: three fit beside the 24 V supply only if each is about 48 mm wide.
TP-Link TL-SF1005D: the PLC, the Raspberry Pi and the laptop on Cat6 cables (parts list 2026-11-09). On the table by the control cabinet, beside the laptop (owner, step 17).
Runs the web app; its screen shows the 3D twin, so the panel has no screen of its own (parts list 2026-11-09; owner, step 17). In front of the control cabinet.
